title: EXPLORE PHYSICAL-PRODUCT AFFILIATE MARKETING WITH CHATGPT
content:
Physical-product affiliate marketing lets you earn from recommendations without buying, storing, or shipping the product yourself. The merchant controls much more of the transaction, which also means your commission depends on the merchant's program and attribution rules.

YOU ARE SELLING THE RECOMMENDATION, NOT OWNING THE PRODUCT
The merchant owns the product and normally handles payment and fulfillment. Your role is helping the right customer discover or choose it.

UNDERSTAND ATTRIBUTION
Your recommendation creates income only according to the program's rules. A customer can appreciate your advice, buy later through another path, and generate no commission. Treat attribution as a business dependency rather than an invisible technical detail.

SPECIFICITY EXAMPLE
Too broad: "I want to be an Amazon affiliate."
More useful: "I want to help families choose practical road-trip gear for young children and earn referral commission on products I recommend."

The merchant or program may change later. The clearer business direction is the customer and buying problem you want to help with.

WHAT PHYSICAL AFFILIATE MARKETING LOOKS LIKE

Suppose you publish a recommendation for a $120 stroller and link to the retailer through an affiliate program.

A reader follows the tracked link and buys the stroller from the retailer. The retailer collects the customer's money, owns or sources the inventory, ships the stroller, handles the retail transaction, and applies its return policies. If the purchase qualifies under the affiliate agreement, you receive a commission.

You did not sell a stroller out of your own inventory. You created a referral that contributed to somebody else's retail sale.

WHY THIS CAN BE LIGHTER OPERATIONALLY

Because the merchant remains the retailer, you generally do not need to buy, store, pack, or ship the physical item. That removes many of the day-to-day workloads that come with resale or dropshipping.

The tradeoff is control. You depend on the merchant's inventory, prices, product pages, checkout, attribution rules, commission rates, and program policies. A product can disappear or a commission can change without your permission.

This makes affiliate marketing especially different from owning a physical-product business even when both businesses talk about exactly the same products.

WHAT YOU SHOULD DECIDE HERE

Physical-product affiliate marketing is worth exploring if the part you want to own is the recommendation rather than the retail operation.

You can build useful content, expertise, comparisons, demonstrations, curation, or other reasons for people to trust your recommendations without becoming the store that stocks and ships every product.

In exchange, you surrender substantial control over the transaction.

A useful result is:

"I want to help this type of customer choose products in this category, and I am comfortable earning through referrals rather than owning the retail sale."

If you find yourself wishing you controlled the price, checkout, customer account, packaging, and reorder relationship, another physical-product model may fit better.

AFFILIATE DISCLOSURE NOTE

Being a referrer rather than the retailer does not remove advertising responsibilities. In the United States, the FTC says compensated endorsers and affiliate marketers should clearly disclose material connections, and endorsements must be truthful and not misleading.

The library does not attempt to prescribe the exact disclosure for every platform or situation. Check current official requirements when you begin promoting products.

HOW TO USE THIS
Use the prompt below to turn this branch into your version of the business. Answer the questions honestly, ask for clarification when you need it, and do not treat external facts as verified just because ChatGPT mentions them.

WHAT THIS INTERVIEW SHOULD PRODUCE

By the end, you should have a plausible product category, customer, and reason your recommendations could be useful, plus a list of affiliate-program facts to verify.

ChatGPT should help determine whether you actually prefer being the recommender rather than the retailer.

It should not drift into a marketing-channel plan. Finding traffic, building an audience, content strategy, and conversion tactics belong to the later How Do I Sell It? work.

COPY & PASTE INTO CHATGPT

During the interview:
- Ask one question at a time unless a small group of tightly related questions is genuinely easier to answer together.
- Use my answers before deciding what to ask next. Do not run through a generic questionnaire when an answer makes a question irrelevant.
- If I say "I don't know," help me identify what I need to decide or research. Do not silently invent an answer for me.
- Explain unfamiliar business terms in plain language when they first become relevant.
- Separate assumptions from facts that require outside verification.
- Do not turn this into a marketing or customer-acquisition plan unless the purpose of this specific interview requires it.
- When you have enough information, stop interviewing me and give me the requested conclusion, including the important unknowns and next research questions.
Ask me one question at a time unless a small group of closely related questions would be easier to answer together. If I say I don't know, help me identify what I would need to decide or research instead of inventing an answer for me.

Interview me to explore a physical-product affiliate direction. Learn who I could help, which product categories are relevant to them, what knowledge or credibility I bring, and what kinds of recommendations I could make genuinely useful.

Help me identify program details to investigate, including commission, attribution windows, whether later purchases are credited, product quality, returns, and merchant dependence. Do not assume a future purchase by the same customer will pay me again.

End with a specific physical-affiliate direction and verification checklist.

NEXT → PDF 46 if clear; PDF 16 to compare another method.

While interviewing me, follow these rules:

Do not start with a retailer or affiliate network. Start with the customer and the buying decisions the user can make easier.

If the user names a program, do not assume attribution, commission, or eligibility terms are current.

At the end, give me:
- Customer
- Physical product category
- Recommendation angle
- Merchant/program characteristics needed
- Attribution questions
- Verification list
- Specific affiliate direction
